info.name: ApiGateway (JACAG-19)
info.description: Run the folders top to bottom (Collection Runner or one by one) against the whole system started with docker compose (only the Gateway on baseUrl is used). Every run uses unique data and removes the profiles it created. The accounts of the registered users stay in the Authentication Service: nothing deletes an account by its login, on purpose. Before the run set the CURRENT values of adminLogin, adminPassword and internalKey (they are secrets and are not stored in this file). Folder 3 runs as the admin, folder 4 checks what the Gateway refuses, folder 5 proves the undoing of a failed registration, folder 6 places orders as two registered users and as the admin (the Order Service, its owner lookup in the User Service and the ownership rules through the Gateway), folder 7 pays an order as a registered user (the outcome of a payment is random, so the payment is repeated until it is SUCCESS), follows the event of the payment to the order and checks the payments, the lists and the totals through the Gateway, folder 8 removes what the run created.

item.name: 73 Anna pays the order (the payment is repeated until it is SUCCESS)

exec: // The status is random, so the payment is repeated until one is SUCCESS. Every attempt is sent with
// the same body (the forged fields included) and judged by the same code. A 502 or a 504 is the
// random number service, which is outside the system, failing or being slow (the first call after
// a start is the slowest: DNS and TLS): the Payment Service saves nothing then, so asking again is
// right, but only MAX_TRANSIENT times. The checks run once, at the end, so their number is fixed.
const state = { requests: 0, saved: 0, transient: [], first: null, last: null, problem: null };
pm.test("A payment is created (201) and its Location points to the Gateway", function () {
pm.test("The payer is the profile of the token; the outcome and the time are the service's own", function () {
pm.test(`The order is paid by a SUCCESS payment (at most ${MAX_REQUESTS} requests, at most ${MAX_TRANSIENT} failures of the random number service)`, function () {
state.problem = `The random number service failed ${state.transient.length} times`;

request.description: The whole chain: Gateway, Payment Service, the random number service (an even number is SUCCESS, an odd one FAILED, both are a 201), MongoDB and the event on Kafka. The outcome is random, so the script repeats the payment (at most 20 requests) until one is SUCCESS; the next requests need a paid order. A 502 or 504 is the random number service failing or being slow (the first call after a start is the slowest); the Payment Service saves nothing then, so the script asks again, at most 3 times. The fields userId, status and timestamp of the body are forged on purpose: the payer is user_id of the token, the outcome comes from the random number service and the time from the clock of the service. A service that took the status from the body would never give SUCCESS and the last check would fail.
